---
title: "Building Websites with Quarto"
---

Learn to turn Markdown and R code into a website, and publish it for free on GitHub Pages. This is how the [NV OSE training site](https://nv-ose.github.io/training/) you're reading right now is built.

## Overview

- **Audience:** Staff who want to publish trainings, documentation, or project sites, or add a training to this site
- **Level:** Beginner to intermediate
- **Duration:** About 2.5 hours (can be split into two sessions)
- **Format:** Workshop or self-paced
- **Editors:** Instructions for **Positron**, **VS Code**, and **RStudio**. Pick your editor once in any tab set, and every page follows your choice.

## Learning objectives

By the end of this training, you will be able to:

1. Explain what Quarto is and how a `.qmd` file becomes a web page.
2. Write a Quarto page with Markdown, callouts, images with alt text, and R code chunks.
3. Create a Quarto website project and organize pages with a navbar and sidebar.
4. Preview and render a site, and fix common errors.
5. Customize the look (themes, light and dark mode, logo, footer) while keeping it accessible.
6. Publish a site on **GitHub Pages**, and update it.
7. Add a new training to the NV OSE training site.

## Prerequisites

- Completed [Introduction to Git and GitHub](../intro-to-github/index.qmd), or comfortable with commits, pushing, and GitHub Desktop
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) installed
- [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) installed, with the `rmarkdown` and `knitr` packages (for pages that run R code)
- An editor: [Positron](https://positron.posit.co/), [VS Code](https://code.visualstudio.com/), or [RStudio](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/)
- A GitHub account and [GitHub Desktop](https://desktop.github.com/download/)

Basic R is helpful but not required. The examples are short and explained.

::: {.callout-note}
On a state computer you may need IT to install Quarto, R, or an editor. Request them ahead of time.
:::
